definitions.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
definitions.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞]. Throughout, a δ-cover means a family covering the set with ediam of every member ≤ofReal δ; the finite-scale real-diameter notation never admits an unbounded member through toReal(∞)=0.

definitions.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. Explicitly, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} C_p(r,B), including all extended positive scales.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, dimH(B)=sup{a∈[0,∞): μH[a](B)=∞}, evaluated in [0,∞] using the Borel measurable structure. The supremum of an empty set of exponents is 0. This is the native Hausdorff dimension with the original critical-exponent convention; the equality of the native measure and the original positive-exponent covering normalization is established in the proof.

For metric spaces Z,Y, maxProd(Z,Y) is Z×Y with distance between (x,t),(y,u) equal to max(dist_Z(x,y),dist_Y(t,u)). For real normed spaces this is the standard max norm on the product. Products in auxiliary propositions use this metric unless explicitly Euclidean.
For a finite dimensional real vector space Z, finrank(Z)=Module.finrank ℝ Z is the natural-number cardinality of any finite basis. Natural values are embedded into [0,∞] in dimension inequalities.
Vn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), identified with ℝ^n with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. Fin n={0,...,n−1}; for n=0 it is empty and Vn consists of the zero tuple.
Wn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)), with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure.

T(x,t) has coordinates T(x,t)(i.castSucc)=x(i) for i∈Fin n and T(x,t)(Fin.last n)=t, where i.castSucc retains the index i<n in Fin(n+1) and Fin.last n is its last index n. This defines a total map without presupposing linearity or invertibility.
Feuc={z∈Wn : (i↦z(i.castSucc))∈E and z(Fin.last n)∈I}. This is exactly the Euclidean product subset E×[0,1] in the original target.

inputs.statement: E is compact in Euclidean ℝ^n.
For every finite dimensional real normed space V and every nonempty compact A⊆V, dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1 in [0,∞], with A×I in maxProd(V,ℝ). This includes finrank(V)=0.

For the original natural n, the coordinate map T:maxProd(Vn,ℝ)→Wn is a real linear equivalence with inverse z↦((i↦z(i.castSucc)),z(Fin.last n)). It maps Fmax exactly onto Feuc, and dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax). For all x,y∈Vn and t,u∈ℝ, setting a=||x−y||₂ and b=|t−u| gives domain distance max(a,b) and target distance sqrt(a²+b²), with max(a,b)≤sqrt(a²+b²)≤sqrt(2)max(a,b). The constants are independent of n,E and points, and all assertions include n=0.

output.statement: dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, with Feuc in Euclidean Wn and E in Euclidean Vn.

argument.text: Apply N006 to V=Vn and A=E. Vn is the Euclidean real normed space with its finite coordinate basis, and the original hypotheses H001,H002 give respectively nonemptiness and compactness. Therefore dimH(Fmax)=dimH(E)+1. N007 gives dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax), with Feuc precisely the original Euclidean product subset in Wn. Substitution yields dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, the complete selected equality for every natural n including zero, with the original Euclidean metrics and no additional hypotheses.
